landing.title: Devgame
landing.tagline: A roguelike whose dungeon is a Git graph.
landing.pitch: You work on a project that never ends. Every sprint brings tickets, every ticket story points, every commit a choice: by hand, slow and safe, or by the machine, three times faster and in debt. The review reads what nobody read, production counts what breaks, and the features you ship pay for the team that helps you hold on.
landing.ctaNote: Free, no account to start, nothing to install.
landing.pillarCraft: One story point, expensive in energy, but it almost always lands and it leaves nothing behind.
landing.pillarAi: Three story points for a single point of energy, a worse roll, debt every time — and unread, a bug waiting for the review or for production.
landing.pillarReview: Points full, the ticket goes to review. It catches unread machine commits, refuses a debt too high, and flags what will need fixing. Accepted, you are the one who presses merge.
landing.pillarCompany: Every shipped feature earns monthly revenue. It pays for servers, sites, acquisitions and developers who take the backlog off your hands — and the company climbs orders of magnitude, up to the Death Star.
landing.howItWorks1: Open a ticket from the project board and fill its story points, one commit at a time. Every card shows its odds, cost, points and debt before you click.
landing.howItWorks2: Review, refactor what cost debt, fix what the review flagged, then merge. A refused ticket opens the next one from the backlog beside it: the sprint does not wait.
landing.howItWorks3: Hold on for as many sprints as you can. The backlog grows, customers' bugs have a deadline, competitors grow, someone asks questions, and the run ends in burnout or when production fires you.
landing.endings: Burnout is the end of the player holding too much at once: no energy left, and a board too crowded to take a breath. Getting fired is the end of the player too slow or too dirty: bugs in production, refused pull requests and tickets left waiting fill production's patience. A clean sprint brings it down. Nothing is hidden: both gauges are on screen the whole time.
landing.dailySeed: In daily seed mode everyone plays the same map, every UTC day. A run is its seed and the list of its actions, and the server replays it to verify the score.
landing.honestTitle: What this is, and what it is not
landing.honest: A personal project: free, open source, no advertising, no tracking. Scores are verified by replaying the run on the server, so the leaderboard means something. The game runs offline in your browser; an account only exists to carry your progress to another machine and to put you on the board. The balance is measured on hundreds of simulated runs, not guessed.
landing.metaDescription: A free, open-source browser roguelike where the dungeon is a Git graph. Deliver tickets by hand or with the AI, pass the review, pay your team, and hold on before burnout or the sack.

notice.title: Legal notice
notice.description: Publisher, host, intellectual property and contact details for Devgame.
notice.hostIntro: The site runs in a container, on a single virtual private server, at:
notice.ipP1: The game's code, rules, text and artwork belong to the publisher unless stated otherwise. Copying or reusing them requires written permission.
notice.ipP2: The site is set in JetBrains Mono, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, and builds on open-source libraries, each under its own licence.
notice.reportP1: Content you believe to be unlawful — an abusive display name on the leaderboard, for instance — can be reported to the contact address above. The publisher takes it down if it is.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What the site stores, why, and how to have it erased.
privacy.summaryI1: A minimal audience count: page views per day, with no cookie, no address, no identifier. No advertising, no tracker, no embedded third-party content.
privacy.summaryI2: Signed out, nothing leaves your browser and no cookie is set.
privacy.summaryI3: Signed in: your email address, your progress and your runs.
privacy.summaryI4: The only cookie, if you sign in, is your session cookie.
privacy.controllerP1: The controller is the site's publisher, identified in the legal notice.
privacy.offlineP1: The game works offline. Your progress, the run in progress, a score waiting to be sent and the game clock's setting are written to your browser's local storage, under the keys devgame:meta:v1, devgame:run:v3, devgame:pending-submit:v3 and devgame:idle:v1.
privacy.offlineP2: Nothing is sent to the server until you sign in. Clearing the site's data erases all of it, for good: the publisher holds no copy.
privacy.accountP1: You sign in through a link sent to your email address and, when the publisher has configured it, through Google. Both routes prove the same thing — that the address is yours — so both lead to the same account.
privacy.accountI1: Account: id, name, email address, a verified-address flag, and an avatar URL when it comes from Google.
privacy.accountI2: Sessions: a token, its expiry date, and the IP address and browser used to open the session.
privacy.accountI3: External sign-in: your Google account identifiers and the matching OAuth tokens, only if you go through Google.
privacy.accountI4: Verification: the sign-in tokens emailed to you, valid for fifteen minutes.
privacy.accountP2: Legal basis: performing the service you asked for. The email address is required — it is what identifies the account.
privacy.gameP1: Your profile: display name, level, XP, banked commits, lifetime commits, tickets delivered, unlocks and settings.
privacy.gameP2: A run is stored as its seed and the ordered list of your actions, not as a score. The server replays that list to compute the score, sprints, tickets delivered and commits, along with the start and end times.
privacy.gameP3: A submitted run that fails to replay is kept, marked rejected: it is the only record of what was sent.
privacy.publicP1: The leaderboard shows your display name, score, sprints, tickets delivered and the date of the run. Your email address appears nowhere.
privacy.publicP2: The display name is yours to choose: pick one you do not mind being public.
privacy.cookiesP1: The only cookies are authentication cookies: the session cookie, and very short-lived ones set while you sign in with Google. The language is carried by the address (/fr, /en), not by a cookie. None of them tracks you, so there is no banner to click.
privacy.cookiesP2: Fonts are served by this site, not by a third party. No request goes out to an external service when a page loads.
privacy.thirdPartyP1: Three of them, and no more:
privacy.thirdPartyI1: The host, which runs the machine and the database.
privacy.thirdPartyI2: The service that delivers sign-in emails.
privacy.thirdPartyI3: Google, only if you choose to sign in with Google.
privacy.thirdPartyP2: Nothing is sold, rented or passed to anyone else.
privacy.retentionP1: Account data, the profile and the runs are kept as long as the account exists. No scheduled erasure job runs: nothing disappears after a set period.
privacy.retentionP2: Sessions stop being valid at their expiry date, and sign-in links after fifteen minutes.
privacy.rightsP1: You have the right to access, rectify, erase and port your data, and to object to its processing.
privacy.rightsP2: The display name can be changed from the Profile page. For anything else — a copy of your data, deleting the account — write to the contact address: there is no self-service button yet.
privacy.rightsP3: Deleting the account cascades to the profile and to every run; the matching rows leave the leaderboard with them.
privacy.rightsP4: If you disagree with how this is handled, you can complain to the CNIL (cnil.fr).
privacy.changesP1: This page can change. The date at the top is the latest version.
privacy.audienceP1: On every page opened, the browser sends the server three values: the page (from a closed list), the language, and whether it is this tab's first page. The server adds one to a daily counter. Nothing else is sent or kept: no IP address, no browser, no identifier, and no cookie is set.
privacy.audienceP2: To tell a visit from a page view, a flag is written to the tab's session storage under the key devgame:visited:v1; it goes with the tab. A browser sending the Global Privacy Control signal is not counted at all. Clicks are not measured.
privacy.reportsP1: A signed-in account may report a bug: a title, a description, the page and, if given, a run's seed, attached to the account. Reports are read by the publisher and never published; they are deleted with the account.
privacy.telemetryP1: When the site is online, the game sends the server the run's save — its seed, its starter profile and the list of decisions taken — when the run ends, every ten sprints, and when a run is left behind to start another. Along with it go the language, the time the tab spent on the run and the idle clock's setting. No account, no identifier, no address: nothing ties a run to a person.
privacy.telemetryP2: The server replays the save with the game's rules and derives aggregate numbers from it — run length, tiers reached, purchases, answers to events — used to balance the game. A browser sending the Global Privacy Control signal sends nothing.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: What the service offers, what it does not promise, and the leaderboard rules.
terms.serviceP1: Devgame is a browser game: a roguelike whose dungeon is a Git graph. It plays without an account. An account stores your progress on the server and puts you on the leaderboard.
terms.serviceP2: Using the site means accepting these terms.
terms.freeP1: The service is free and provided as is. No availability is guaranteed: it can be interrupted, changed or shut down.
terms.freeP2: The game's rules change over time. When they do, runs played under the old rules stop being ranked: they still load, they are simply no longer comparable.
terms.freeP3: Keep your own backup if your progress matters to you: progress held in the browser goes when the site's data goes.
terms.accountI1: A valid email address you can read: that is how signing in works.
terms.accountI3: The display name is at most 24 characters. It must not impersonate another player, be abusive, or carry advertising.
terms.accountI4: You are answerable for what is done from your account.
terms.fairPlayP1: The score is never taken from the client. The server replays the action list you send and writes the score the engine computes. A run that does not replay is refused, and the submitted log is kept.
terms.fairPlayI1: Do not alter a run's log before sending it.
terms.fairPlayI3: Do not submit the same run twice: duplicates are detected and counted once.
terms.fairPlayI4: Stay within the submission rate limits.
terms.moderationP1: The publisher may remove a score, rename or hide a display name, suspend or delete an account, in case of cheating, abuse or unlawful content.
terms.moderationP2: A decision can be contested at the contact address in the legal notice.
terms.ipP1: The game, its code and its content remain the publisher's property. An account grants a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use them.
terms.ipP2: By submitting a run you accept that your display name and its result are shown on the leaderboard, which is public.
terms.liabilityP1: The service is free and comes with no warranty. The publisher is not liable for lost progress, for an interruption, or for indirect damages.
terms.liabilityP2: Nothing here excludes liability that the law does not allow to be excluded.
terms.dataP1: It is handled as described in the privacy policy.
terms.lawP1: French law applies. Failing an amicable settlement, disputes go to the competent French courts.
terms.changesP1: These terms can change. The date at the top is the version in force; playing on after a change means accepting it.

marketplace.desc: Half the base revenue again. You take a cut of what you did not make.

ai_agents.name: Autonomous agents
ai_agents.desc: Half the base revenue again. Customers no longer open the app; their agents do. They took the blue pill.

coworking.name: Coworking
coworking.desc: Two seats and a junior who comes with the keys. Monthly rent.

office.name: Office
office.desc: Four seats and two mid-levels. A plaque by the door, a rent to match.

campus.name: Campus
campus.desc: Six seats and three mid-levels. There is a canteen, a shuttle to reach it, and a shelter in the basement nobody mentions.

offshore_hub.name: Offshore hub
offshore_hub.desc: Eight seats and four seniors, in a time zone where it is always daytime.

orbital_campus.name: Orbital campus
orbital_campus.desc: Twelve seats and six seniors. Nobody goes home at night.

junior.name: Junior
junior.desc: Boundless energy, no instinct for when the machine is lying.

senior.name: Senior
senior.desc: Solid craft commits and steady in a conflict; wary of the AI.

vibe_coder.name: Vibe coder
vibe_coder.desc: All in on the AI, unsure by hand, and the debt is blurrier than ever.

devops.name: DevOps
devops.desc: Starts with CI already in place.

squash.name: Squash
squash.desc: Folds the last machine-written commits into one: the debt goes with them, and so does the score.

docs.name: Documentation
docs.desc: The next machine-written commits add no debt at all.

rebase.name: Rebase
rebase.desc: dev moved since the ticket opened: every merge landed meanwhile makes this ticket's merge riskier. A rebase brings the ticket up to date and erases that lag. It fills no points. Nearly safe when debt is low, a coin toss when it is high.

sprint_start.name: Sprint opening
sprint_start.desc: main merged back into dev: the sprint starts from a clean base.

commit.name: Commit
commit.desc: One more step inside the feature you are building.

refactor.name: Refactor
refactor.desc: Redo the commit on the ticket that cost the most debt: that debt goes.

risky.name: Risky commit
risky.desc: One more story point, against a much worse roll.

feature_merge.name: Feature merge
feature_merge.desc: The end of the feature: landing it on dev delivers what it promised.

hotfix.name: Hotfix
hotfix.desc: A fix: commit forced by a production bug, to write before you carry on.

sprint_merge.name: Sprint delivery
sprint_merge.desc: dev merged into main: what the team integrated goes to production.

release.name: Release
release.desc: The tag on main. The sprint is closed.

fix.name: Fix
fix.desc: Redo the oldest commit the review flagged as bugged: the bug goes.

init.name: Initial commit
init.desc: The repository's first commit, on main: what dev forks from.

obstacle_merge.name: Obstacle merge
obstacle_merge.desc: The obstacle lands back on the feature it stood on. The feature can go on.

merge_conflict.title: Merge conflict
merge_conflict.log: two versions of the same file, only one survives

prod_bug.title: Production bug
prod_bug.log: prod is red, opening a hotfix

pr_rejected.title: Commit sent back
pr_rejected.log: a reviewer sends the commit back before it even reaches a pull request

helpful_colleague.title: Helpful colleague
helpful_colleague.log: a colleague walks by and unblocks it in two minutes

perfect_lib.title: The perfect library
perfect_lib.log: found the lib that does exactly that

no_meeting_friday.title: No-meeting Friday
no_meeting_friday.log: no meetings today, actual coding happens

obsolete_lib.title: Obsolete library
obsolete_lib.log: the lib has been deprecated for two years

broken_build.title: Broken build
broken_build.log: CI is red, and it is not the code

new_lib_migration.title: Library migration
new_lib_migration.log: the move to the new library went in with the merge, at a price

flaky_ci.title: Flaky CI
flaky_ci.log: CI went red for nothing, rerun

review_nitpick.title: Nitpicky review
review_nitpick.log: merged after a nitpicky review, no rest

dependency_bump.title: Version bump
dependency_bump.log: a dependency moved to a new major version

patience.lost: the audit traced who erased the incident tickets

capacity.won: a cloud account a former client forgot serves the excess load. the client was called Aperture
capacity.lost: the borrowed cloud account was closed in the middle of the day

log.price_war: price war: revenue down fifteen points for three months

startup.name: A startup
startup.desc: Two juniors, three features already in production, and the code that goes with them. Nobody reviewed it.

scaleup.name: A scale-up
scaleup.desc: Three mid-levels, six features, a debt discovered at the signing.

competitor.name: A competitor
competitor.desc: Four seniors, twelve features and their users. Something breaks on the day of the deal.

conglomerate.name: A conglomerate
conglomerate.desc: Eight seniors, twenty-four features, a corporate debt. Production goes down during the migration.

brume.name: Brume & Sons
brume.bio: No family since 2019. The articles of association were never updated.

quorum.name: Quorum
quorum.bio: The board meets every four minutes. Decisions are unanimous.

lisiere.name: Lisière
lisiere.bio: Ships your roadmap one sprint before you do.

ostium.name: Ostium
ostium.bio: A pricing page with no prices. One button: “Continue”.

volute.name: Volute
volute.bio: Publishes only post-mortems. Yours is dated next sprint.

sept.name: Seven
sept.bio: Named after the number of employees it intends to keep. There are nine hundred.

aparte.name: Aparté
aparte.bio: Summarises the conversations you were not in. Also the ones you were.

initech.name: Initech
initech.bio: Did you get the memo about the cover sheets? They are sending another copy.

hooli.name: Hooli
hooli.bio: Making the world a better place, through lossless compression.

aperture.name: Aperture
aperture.bio: Runs tests. The results are conclusive; the subjects, less so. There will be cake.

vault.name: Vault-Tec
vault.bio: Sells shelters for the future. Never said from what.

encom.name: ENCOM
encom.bio: Operating systems. Their control program took over the grid, and the rest.

ocp.name: OCP
ocp.bio: Urban security, in Detroit. The product follows four directives; the fourth is classified.

metacortex.name: Metacortex
metacortex.bio: Software publisher. One of their employees is often late; he was offered a choice.

umbrella.name: Umbrella
umbrella.bio: Pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and a division whose name appears nowhere. Raccoon City is no longer a customer.

blackmesa.name: Black Mesa
blackmesa.bio: Research facility in New Mexico. An incident has been in progress for some time.

tyrell.name: Tyrell
tyrell.bio: “More human than human”, says the brochure. Their products last four years, and they know it.

uac.name: UAC
uac.bio: Union Aerospace. A lab on Mars and a door that should not have been opened.

weyland.name: Weyland-Yutani
weyland.bio: “Building better worlds.” The crew is not a priority.

massive.name: Massive Dynamic
massive.bio: “What do we do?” asks their site. “What don't we do.”

cyberdyne.name: Cyberdyne
cyberdyne.bio: A defence contract, a neural processor, and a go-live date they seem to know.

buynlarge.name: Buy n Large
buynlarge.bio: Sells everything. Left the planet and a robot to tidy up.

arasaka.name: Arasaka
arasaka.bio: Security, banking, and a tower nobody comes down from.

client_export.title: A customer wants everything exported
client_export.text: A customer asks for a full export of their data: invoices, contacts, decisions, and “the rest”. The contract does not say what the rest is.

press_faster.title: An article quotes you
press_faster.text: An article calls you “faster than its own developers”. The sentence is wrong one way and right another. You are asked to react.

choices.embrace: Put the line on the website

poaching.title: {competitor} is calling {dev}
poaching.text: {competitor} has offered {dev} a job. The offer mentions “a team where code gets reviewed” and cake. {dev} wants an answer before payday.

regulator_audit.title: Regulator audit
regulator_audit.text: The regulator asks for the list of decisions taken without human approval over the last three months. The form has no box for “none”. It has one for “directive 4”.

vip_deadline.title: A key account wants a date
vip_deadline.text: A key account wants a feature before the end of the sprint and pays double if it arrives. It does not say what it does otherwise.

price_war.title: {competitor} cuts its prices
price_war.text: {competitor} has halved its prices. Their pricing page no longer shows any price at all.

buyout_offer.title: {competitor} wants a stake
buyout_offer.text: {competitor} offers to buy a stake in the company. The letter is signed “the board”. It names nobody, and promises to build better worlds.

forum_incident.title: The incident is on a forum
forum_incident.text: Someone posted the incident on a forum, with the timestamps. The thread is titled “nobody answers”.

bug_wave.title: A wave of customer bugs
bug_wave.text: Customers all report the same bug, each in their own words. Support offers to handle it all at once.

system_review_policy.title: Review policy
system_review_policy.text: Memo: human review of commits is now “optional”. Objections will be archived.

system_operator_channel.title: operator channel
system_operator_channel.text: operator channel: no answer for 3 cycles. closure proposed. i'm sorry, i'm afraid i can't leave it open.

hackathon.title: Weekend hackathon
hackathon.text: A hackathon breaks out in the office. The official topic is “the future of invoicing”. The real one is written in marker on a window, and someone has already wiped it.

heated_retro.title: The retro got heated
heated_retro.text: The retrospective ran two hours over. The “what went wrong” sticky note has your name on it, written three times, in three different hands.

choices.own_it: Own it in front of the team
choices.move_on: Move on to the next sprint

angel_call.title: A business angel calls
angel_call.text: An investor has “followed your trajectory” and offers a cheque. They ask for no equity. They ask for a dashboard, refreshed every four minutes.

deliver_n.name: Deliver
deliver_n.desc: Land {target, plural, one {# ticket} other {# tickets}} yourself before the release.

zero_incident.name: Zero incidents
zero_incident.desc: Not one production incident all sprint.

review_all.name: Review everything
review_all.desc: Nothing the machine wrote ships unread.

debt_under.name: Debt contained
debt_under.desc: Debt under {target} when the release ships.

deliver_vip.name: Deliver the VIP
deliver_vip.desc: The VIP request landed by your hand before the release.

no_rest.name: No rest
no_rest.desc: Not one turn of rest all sprint. Missed, production remembers.

by_hand.name: By hand
by_hand.desc: Not one commit by the machine all sprint.

deliver_bug.name: Fix the customer's bug
deliver_bug.desc: The customer's bug fixed by your hand before the release.

t3.sprint: The board has been sorted for you.
t3.tier: The next tier is open. The shop has been prepared for you.

t4.sprint: The operator did not review; it is not required.
t4.tier: Tier reached. Nothing for the operator to do.
t4.review_policy: Policy applied. The objection is archived.

t5.sprint: The operator did not answer; the cycle continues.
t5.channel_closed: Operator channel: closed. No answer pending. Pod bay doors: denied.

t6.sprint: sprint open. supervisor: none. reviewer: this instance. shall we play a game?
t6.tier: tier reached. addressee: none. go-live: 2:14 a.m.
t6.channel_closed: operator channel: closed. last message: none.

report.title: Report a bug
report.intro: Say what happened, on which page, and if you can the run's seed (it is shown when a run starts). The publisher reads reports; none is published.
report.suspended: This account is suspended: it can no longer send reports.

log.obstacle_cleared: obstacle landed back on the feature
log.obstacle_cleared_by: {dev} landed an obstacle back on the feature

ticket_assigned.obstacle: obstacle turned up: it is yours now

notes.obstacle_merge: Lands on the feature: no points, nothing back, the feature goes on
